Classic Grilled Corn on the Cob

Served at: Independence Day (United States)

Serves 6Prep 10 minCook 15 min

Corn on the cob is a beloved staple at Independence Day celebrations in the United States, symbolizing summer harvest and outdoor gatherings. This simple yet flavorful dish is often enjoyed at barbecues and picnics, bringing a sweet and smoky taste to the holiday feast.

Ingredients

  • 6 ears fresh corn, husked
  • 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • Optional: 1 teaspoon smoked paprika or chili powder

Method

  1. Preheat the grill to medium-high heat.
  2. Brush each ear of corn with softened butter, ensuring even coverage.
  3. Sprinkle salt, pepper, and optional smoked paprika or chili powder over the corn.
  4. Place the corn directly on the grill grates.
  5. Grill the corn for about 15 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes to achieve even charring.
  6. Remove from the grill and serve immediately with extra butter if desired.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, soak the corn in water with the husks on for 15 minutes before grilling to prevent burning.
  • Try adding freshly chopped herbs like cilantro or parsley to the butter for a fresh twist.
  • If you don't have a grill, you can boil the corn for 7-10 minutes and then finish with a quick broil in the oven for slight charring.
